_note: uv sync --extra crafter (crafter-gym, gym/crafter/, pulls crafter), then pip install --force-reinstall 'crafter @ git+https://github.com/chengfanbrain/crafter.git@deterministic' -- a fork of 1.8.3 whose single change is that a seed plus an action list replays exactly. Plain PyPI crafter runs this config fine and plays identically to a subject, but its blocks cannot be replayed, so a model cannot be given the same episode. This is the paradigm's level 3 (predation): level 2 plus the things that fight back. Zombies come out of the dark and skeletons shoot from the caves, so the subject is managing a homeostat and a threat at once, which is the one thing this level adds. The rules are the env's (gym/crafter/crafter_gym/levels.py, 'level' in env_kwargs below) and not this file's, so a model meets the same game: see _level_note.
_shared_notes: Every field of the game phase below is level 4's, except env_kwargs.level, resume, and the page above the game. The notes that explain those shared fields -- the eight buttons and the menu, turn-based pacing, frame size, savestate stride, the live HUD, the score line, the three cues, and why there is one interface for all of them -- are in configs/dbp_games/crafter__crafter_L4.json and are deliberately not copied here, because four copies of a paragraph drift apart and the one thing a level is allowed to change is the game.
_level_note: The level is a gymnasium.Wrapper under the menu (crafter_gym.levels.LevelWrapper), and the table it reads is the rig's own (crafter-for-brain-scan v0.33, core.py:LEVELS), field for field. L3 is hostiles=True, homeostatic_death=True, hidden_items=(), so the game itself is stock crafter and what separates it from level 4 is what is written down in this file: the paradigm runs the two as different levels because level 3 still has the task chain and level 4 is free play, which is in fmri-gym now (see _tasks_note). So a level-3 block and a level-4 block differ in their resume slot and in the chain above the frame -- fifteen entries named one at a time against none -- and in nothing else a subject can see, which is worth knowing before a pilot is designed around them. Death itself is unchanged in every level: health cannot regenerate from 0 (stock crafter can add a point on the very tick a death set it there, which would make the episode's end unreliable), and the view is tinted red while the player is dead, which is the engine's own commented-out tint. The same seed gives the same terrain in all four levels, hostiles included, since a peaceful level is the same world with its hostiles deleted afterwards.
_tasks_note: The task chain is on here because the level names tasks (crafter_gym.levels.LEVELS), and this phase names no 'tasks' field, so the two completion messages are held for the rig's own defaults. What the chain is, what it counts, and what a hold costs the block's clock are in crafter__crafter_L1.json:_tasks_note, which is the one level that sets the field. L4 names no tasks, so the chain is the second thing a subject can see between these two levels, after the hostiles. This level's homeostat runs, so it carries the chain's three low-stat interrupts as well (LEVELS: stat_tasks, the same fifteen entries as L2): drink water, eat a cow and sleep, each asked for the first time its stat is seen at or below 8 of 9. They are the one errand here that a subject can be interrupted by while something is also hunting them, which is the pair of demands this level exists to ask about.
_not_here_note: Nothing of the rig's task system is missing now; the two ways the interrupts deliberately differ from the rig's are in crafter__crafter_L1.json:_not_here_note.
_resume_note: resume names the thread of play this block continues, and the block picks up the world the last block of the same name left off in, but only when the block's clock was what stopped the episode: a death or a forfeit ends that world and the next block opens a new one from its seed. Dying has to keep costing what crafter charges for it, and on a level whose deaths are something the world did that matters more than anywhere else; the world is carried so that the scanner's clock does not change the game, not so that death stops mattering. The name is this level's own, because all four levels are the same env id (CrafterMenu-v0) and one shared name would hand L4's world to an L3 block -- which on this level would be invisible, since the two play the same rules today. The level is carried in env_kwargs, so it is in the slot file's header too: a block whose level does not match the world it is about to continue is told so by name before it plays (fmri_gym/resume.py:env_drift). What comes back is the world's own rules and not this config's, because restore replaces the env the block just built -- which is the whole reason a level is a wrapper's parameter and not a patch an adapter applies to a live player.
_instructions_note: The page is level 4's with its opening lines replaced by the rig's own (core.py:INSTRUCTIONS page 1, plus the single line core.py:LEVEL_INTROS gives this level). The controls are the same eight buttons and the same menu, so a subject who practised in the rig keeps their fingers. One line of what this level is about and nothing more -- 'some additional dangers' names no creature and no tactic, because what a rule does is the game's job to show. The rig shows that line between levels ('The next rounds are different'), and a config played on its own has to say it up front instead.

text: Explore the world and try things.
The game itself will show you what works.
The world waits for you: it moves one step each
time you press a button, and not otherwise.
The menu holds the ten actions with no button of
their own: place stone, table, furnace, plant, and
make a wood / stone / iron pickaxe or sword. W
moves the cursor and shows it over your character;
A performs it. Moving the cursor also costs a turn.
